{{Short description|German academic}}
'''Anke Blume''' (b. 6 April 1969<ref name="cv">{{cite web |title=PROF.DR. A. BLUME (ANKE) FULL PROFESSOR |url=https://people.utwente.nl/a.blume |website=utwente.nl |publisher=U Twente |access-date=11 February 2023}}</ref>) is an engineering technology professor at the [[University of Twente]] known for her contributions to [[silica]] and [[silane]] chemistry for rubber applications.<ref name="rpn22">{{cite news |title=ACS Rubber Division names 2023 Science and Technology Award winners |url=https://www.rubbernews.com/news/acs-rubber-division-names-2023-science-and-technology-award-winners |access-date=15 November 2022 |work=Rubber News |publisher=Crain |date=11 November 2022}}</ref>

== Education ==
Anke Blume was born in [[Hanover]], Germany, April 6, 1969.<ref name="cv" />
Blume studied chemistry at [[Leibniz University]] in Hannover, earning a master's degree in July 1993. She went on to complete doctoral studies at the [[German Institute for Rubber Technology]] (DIK), finishing in 1995 and continuing for a 9-month term as a post-doc.<ref name="ieee">{{cite web |title=Anke Blume |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37086461120 |website=[[IEEE]] |publisher=IEEE |access-date=11 February 2023}}</ref>

== Career ==

Blume began an industrial career in 1996 as a chemist with the product development group at silica supplier Degussa AG (later to become Evonik).  In 2011, she managed intellectual property for silica and silane in rubber applications.

Blume's academic career began when she joined the University of Twente in 2013, as Chair of Elastomer Technology and Engineering (ETE) Group.  She has been noted for her contributions to rubber technology aimed at {{CO2}} reduction, in particular for automotive [[lightweighting]] and for tire [[rolling resistance]] reduction.<ref name="phys14">{{cite news |last1=Vreeman |first1=Jochem |title=Rubber technology important in reducing {{CO2}} emissions |url=https://phys.org/news/2014-09-rubber-technology-important-co2-emissions.html |access-date=11 February 2023 |work=phys.org |publisher=Science X Network |date=23 September 2014}}</ref> She was invited to a jury that judged [[Nokian Tyres]] sustainability innovation challenge.<ref name="helsinki22">{{cite news |title=Nokian Tyres reveals the members of their sustainability innovation challenge grand jury |url=https://www.helsinkitimes.fi/business/21073-nokian-tyres-reveals-the-members-of-their-sustainability-innovation-challenge-grand-jury.html |access-date=11 February 2023 |work=Helsinki Times |date=14 Feb 2022}}</ref>  She also served on the panel that selected the Tire Technology International Awards for Innovation and Excellence.<ref name="tti19">{{cite news |last1=Evans |first1=Rachel |title=Tire Technology International Awards for Innovation and Excellence Winners – announced |url=https://www.tiretechnologyinternational.com/news/awards/tire-technology-international-awards-for-innovation-and-excellence-winners.html |access-date=11 February 2023 |work=Tire Technology International |publisher=UKi Media |date=8 March 2019}}</ref>  Blume was elected to serve as head of the German Rubber Society's western group, DKG West, for the term 2018–2021.<ref name="dkg">{{cite news |title=Prof. Anke Blume heads DKG West |url=https://www.gummibereifung.de/prof-anke-blume-leitet-dkg-west |access-date=11 February 2023 |work=www.gummibereifung.de/ |publisher=DKG |date=20 September 2018}}</ref>

==Awards==
